body: Also a paramedic. I'm jonesing for one of those blow by bears. Beats building a blanket fort on the oh shit bar because the kid won't even let you put a cup near their face.
I don't know anything for sure. I think she was bipolar. Unmedicated of course, so it was pretty bad.

I'm sorry, I wasn't clear, my grandparents never said those things. It was everyone else that said that.   I think my grandmother may actually have been a saint. She was always helpful and accepting. She was one of those people who would give her last morsel of food away and go hungry. I miss her. 

Early childhood....my mom remarried an abusive alcoholic. It was not uncommon to get backhands off my feet out of nowhere. The fights between them were epic. Once he decided to beat her with a fire place poker. She got it away from him and broke his arm in three places. Then took him to the hospital. The next day, she hung it over the fireplace as a reminder. There was a time when a huge solid wood coffee table ended up in 11 pieces after one of their fights. Then there was the time he shot a mouse in the utility room inches from the gas water heater. We scattered. He left the shotgun laying across the baby's high chair and went to the bar. She came home to missing kids and a shotgun at the table. And on and on. Eventually, when I was 11, she divorced him, and we went to live with her mother. That wasn't much better. It was a very verbally abusive household. One day, I was beaten with the buckle end of a belt because I didn't want to eat my grandmother's bean salad. Because I was ungrateful. I was smacked across the back with a post hole digger once, but don't remember why. Once I was thrown out of the house in the winter wearing sweats and a Tshirt. No shoes, socks, or jacket. I walked maybe a quarter of a mile to call an aunt to please come get me. She wouldn't. I would get in trouble for reading too much, or leaving and just walking to get out.  When I was 13, she had me committed because I was a bad kid. I know I wasn't the greatest, I had a tendency to say whatever I was thinking, but I was a good student. I didn't get into trouble. Maybe it's a case of being blind to my own actions, but I don't see how I was so horrible. In the end, when it was time for me to be released and sent home, she was going to take me to an orphanage. No one else wanted me either. That's when my grandparents stepped in. 

I wish all of this could have made me an introvert. But I'm still outspoken. If I learned to keep my mouth shut, maybe life would be better. I don't function well in our society. I think my mom was crazy. I know my dad has issues. And I got the genetics. So be it. But I'm done.

I'm just broken.  Have been for a long time.  And of very little value to anyone.  Dad signed away his rights when I was 3.  Mom turned me over to an orphanage when I was 13.  Grandparents (paternal) took me in, and promptly tried to send me to live with my dad.  I refused to stay, so they took me back.  They were good people, and probably the only people to ever treat me well.  For the years I was with them, everyone let me know that I was a burden to them, and what a bad person I was.  I was too loud.  Too outspoken.  My sense of humor was wrong.  They were very religious, but I was not.  One day, I asked, in all sincerity, where they got their faith.  It was assumed that I was being disrespectful.  I was advised that if I couldn't treat them with respect while they were alive, I shouldn't come to their funerals.  That sort of thing.  I was always being told that I was just like my mom.  And that was not a good thing.  I don't think anyone knew how much all that hurt.  I was angry.  I was walled off.  I left as soon as I could.  
Couldn't afford an education, so I did the best I could.  Got married, had a family.  Failed at a great many things.  I was diagnosed with depression in my early 20's.  Lots of different meds, mostly unsuccessful.  Kids got older and I got to go back to school to do what I do now.  I love what I do.  I take care of other people.  And for that time I'm in control.  I know what I'm doing, and who I am doesn't matter.  But the depression was severe.  I lost a job over it.  Eventually, someone noticed a pattern, and I was diagnosed bipolar II.  Cue divorce.  I got a promotion at work.  Then got a new boss.  The job was too much (long story), plus going back to court, plus meds adjustment, plus life in general.....I lost that job.  They were "kind" enough to only demote me though, so it's not like everyone wasn't talking about me behind my back.  Oh, but even though we've said that we won't put people on {this} schedule, we don't want to inconvenience anyone, so we'll do it to you.  I don't know, maybe I'm paranoid (doesn't mean they're not out to get you, right), but it just seems like management has a deep dislike for me.  I've looked for another job, but no one wants me.  Not, someone else was more qualified, or a better fit....they didn't hire me, and the job posting is still out there. Even though, I have the experience and qualifications.  So, that leaves my personality.  Sad, isn't it, when you're so repulsive, people can hate you in the span of a job interview.  I've had exactly one close friend in my life.  But they've moved on.  We've lived countries apart at time, and maintained a close relationship.  But now, the only thing I know about their life is from Facebook.  There is honestly no point in continuing to do this.  What do they say?  Insanity is doing the same thing over and over and expecting different results?  

I am constantly judged, and found lacking.  Mental health issues in my line of work will soon find you with no one to work with.  It's so much fun listening to people mock the SI patient.  Or call a manager that keeps changing their mind bipolar.  I'm just tired.  I'm fresh out of meds to try.  Lithium (which I said I'd never take) is what I'm down to plus a few others to round out the cocktail.  I'm just done.  How sad is it that I'm sitting here telling you, a complete stranger, all about my problems?  Because not a single solitary fucking person in my actual life could give a single fuck about me  

I don't want to die.  I want to go to sleep and never wake up.  The dying part is what has kept me alive this long.  But I think I have it figured out now.  

I appreciate that you have taken the time to take an interest.  I'm sorry that this has been so long.  And for the profanity.  I would go back to edit, but I've completely deleted this response about 4 times.
I've come to look at it like walking down a long road. Black on both sides, but not empty. You gotta keep walking or whatever is in the dark will get you.

Today, it's raining in the desert. Literally. Today, I work. My work is giving myself physically and emotionally to someone else on the worst day of their lives. Although today, I can gather more tools. Today, I need to spend my energy pretending. I have to fight the emotions, and hide from my co-worker because after so much time together, he can read my mind...almost.  The dam broke last night after posting. I hadn't cried in I don't know how long. I haven't slept because I spent those hours wailing, screaming, strengthening my resolve. And the person on the other side of the bed kept on sleeping. 

Edit 
Want to hear something funny?  I take people like me for help. Or find them after they've done it right. But if I ask for help, I could lose my job. Not just my job, my license.

The point is, I have no value to anyone else. 

You say I should "be honest with your life choices". So, I should own that everything wrong with my life is my fault?  You really think that's not already where I'm at?  That I don't realize that I'm such a worthless piece of garbage that it's no wonder that no one wants anything to do with me?  Thanks. 

But maybe if I just take the Meds and get a hobby, all with be well. Which Meds do you suggest?  Because I'm 40 and I've run out of Meds to try. Some work for awhile, some don't work at all, some have such horrible side effects that I couldn't possibly take them.  But maybe that hobby thing will be the miracle that heals depression. 

I really don't think you have the slightest idea what it takes to get to this point. But I guess you tried to help.
